events.text: Analyst request: several cards this month show purchases from the same unusual device profile. Review transaction 3478561 on card C13487-K1 and look for related activity.

events.msg: Core toolkit: flagged transaction, card window, card baseline, recurring charges, resolved account history, device neighbours, region activity and prior cases

hypotheses: Account Takeover (ATO) as part of a coordinated fraud ring sharing a specific device profile and routing through anonymous proxies
Legitimate transaction by the cardholder using a newly acquired device that happens to share a profile with other users
Card testing or credential stuffing activity targeting this card and others using the same device signature

calls.why: To identify the other 19 cards and customers sharing this specific device profile, and to check if any of those accounts have confirmed fraud cases.
To examine the full transaction history of card C13487-K1 around the flagged date to check for other unusual online activity or signs of compromise.

events.msg: Four specialist analysts reviewing their evidence in parallel

events.assessment: The flagged transaction 3478561 on card C13487-K1 represents a highly suspicious departure from the card's established baseline. The card primarily transacts in-person (69 out of 71 baseline transactions) for product 'W', whereas the flagged transaction is an online purchase for product 'C' using an anonymous proxy and a 'New' device profile that has been linked to 114 other transactions across the system.
key_points: Transaction 3478561 is an online transaction for $74.96, contrasting with the card's historical baseline of 97% in-person transactions.
The transaction utilized an anonymous proxy ('IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS') and a specific, non-generic mobile device profile ('SM-G935F Build/NRD90M...') marked as 'New' for this card.
The associated device profile is highly active across the system, appearing in 114 transactions, indicating a shared device or emulator environment used by a fraud ring.

events.assessment: The transaction on card C13487-K1 was executed using a fully specified mobile device profile flagged as 'New' and routing through an anonymous proxy. Given the lack of prior history on this card account and the high-risk device attributes, this transaction is highly suspicious.
key_points: Card account C13487-K1 has only one recorded transaction on 2016-11-22 16:11:00.
The transaction used a specific mobile device profile (SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080) flagged as 'New'.
The connection utilized an anonymous proxy (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS), masking the true location of the user.

events.assessment: The target transaction is part of a large-scale network of 52 cards sharing the same device profile, all utilizing anonymous proxies (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS) to conduct transactions. The high volume of distinct cards (such as C10326-K1, C13487-K1, and C09049-K1) registering this device profile as 'New' within a short timeframe strongly indicates a coordinated card-testing or card-not-present fraud ring.
key_points: A single device profile is shared by 52 distinct cards all-time, with multiple transactions occurring within days of each other.
All associated transactions, including 3460634 on card C13487-K1 and 3457285 on card C10326-K1, utilize an anonymous proxy (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS).
Every transaction in this network is flagged as a 'New' device for the respective card, indicating unauthorized access or card-not-present fraud rather than legitimate shared usage.

events.assessment: The investigation into transaction 3478561 on card C13487-K1 cannot be completed because the provided database queries returned no transaction, customer, or device records. Without this evidence, we are unable to verify the existence of the unusual device profile or link it to other cards.
key_points: The query returned no closed cases or similar patterns associated with the customer or transaction.
No transaction details, device profiles, or card history for C13487-K1 were provided in the evidence.

The same device profile (SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080) was used on 19 other card(s) of 19 other customer(s) between 2016-11-14 and 2016-11-22, 24 of those uses as a New device, 24 behind an anonymising proxy. events.what_would_change_verdict: If the shared device profile were generic (missing model, OS, or screen resolution) rather than fully specified, it could not be used as evidence of coordinated abuse. This would lower the fraud probability and remove the justification for FILE_REPORT, MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS, and ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST under R6 and R9.
